title: Toot-Toot, Right Beside You
moral: Even the biggest ones feel better with a friend right beside them.
summary: On a quiet evening at the harbor, {{child}} and Pip the little tugboat help Big Gray, an enormous and very shy ship, find the courage to come in to the dock. A gentle story about being small, being brave, and staying close.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Toot-toot! The little sound bounced across the harbor, and {{child}} looked up from the end of the dock. There, bobbing on the water, was Pip — the smallest tugboat in the whole town, painted red with one bright yellow stripe.

segments.speaker: Pip
segments.text: {{child}}! Will you help me? There's a ship out there who won't come in.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Far out past the lighthouse sat a ship so big it looked like a gray hill floating on the sea. It wasn't moving. Not one bit. Its lights blinked slowly, the way eyes blink when someone isn't sure.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: So {{child}} climbed aboard, and Pip puttered out across the water. Putt-putt-putt. The waves went slap, slap against the side. The big ship grew bigger, and bigger, and bigger still.

segments.speaker: Big Gray
segments.text: Oh, hello. I'm sorry. The harbor is so narrow, and I am so very wide. What if I bump something?

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: {{child}} looked up, up, up at the giant ship. Then {{child}} had an idea, and whispered it to Pip.

segments.speaker: Pip
segments.text: Big Gray, we'll go slow. You won't be alone for a single wave. Toot-toot — I'm right beside you.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Pip nudged up close to Big Gray's side. Gently. Gently. And very slowly, the enormous ship began to move. Past the lighthouse. Toot-toot — right beside you.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Past the fishing boats, all tucked up for the night. Toot-toot — right beside you. Past the sleepy seagulls on their posts, who opened one eye and closed it again.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And then — bump. The softest bump in the world. Big Gray was home at the dock, safe and still.

segments.speaker: Big Gray
segments.text: I did it. We did it. Thank you, little ones.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: The harbor grew quiet. The water went hush, hush against the dock. Big Gray's lights dimmed, one by one, like a giant settling into bed.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Pip carried {{child}} back to shore and gave one last, tiny toot. {{child}} walked home, warm and sleepy, and as the night wrapped around the harbor, a little sound drifted across the water. Toot-toot. Right beside you. Always.
